description: Communities exposed to pollution should shape environmental biotechnology use.
Agricultural biotechnology must protect farmer voice seed sovereignty and biodiversity.
Biosurveillance requires privacy trust consent and accountability.
Biomanufacturing should be assessed for local benefit labor and ecological impacts.
Synthetic biology needs public oversight and benefit sharing beyond technical review.
Advanced therapies can deepen inequality without equitable financing and access design.
AI-enabled biology may concentrate design power without shared governance.
Genome editing governance must include disability justice and affected communities.
